Use a force F to pull small ball b so that both small balls are in a state of rest, and the angle between the thin string OA and the vertical direction remains $\theta{=}30^{\circ}$. Then the minimum value of F is (　　)

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: After two small balls a and b, both of mass m, are connected with a thin string, they are then suspended from point O with a thin string, as shown in the figure. Use a force F to pull small ball b so that both small balls are in a state of rest, and the angle between the thin string OA and the vertical direction remains $\theta=30^{\circ}$. What is the minimum value of F?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, the upper part is fixed point O, and the thin string OA connects obliquely downward to the right from point O to small ball a; a vertical dashed line is drawn at point O, and the angle between OA and the vertical direction is marked as θ. Small ball a is then connected by another thin string to small ball b at the lower right, and small ball b is subjected to an external force F obliquely upward to the right. The problem states that the masses of the two small balls are both m, and θ=30°. Reasoning: Regard small balls a and b and the thin string between them as one whole, then the tension of the thin string between a and b is an internal force and may be disregarded. The external forces on the whole are: the tension of the upper thin string OA, with direction along OA; the total gravity of the two balls 2mg, with direction vertically downward; and the external force F. Take the direction perpendicular to OA to analyze equilibrium. Since the tension of OA is along OA, its component in the direction perpendicular to OA is 0. The angle between the direction of gravity and OA equivalently gives the component in the direction perpendicular to OA; the magnitude of this component of each small ball’s gravity is mg sinθ, so the magnitude of the component of the total gravity of the two balls in the direction perpendicular to OA is 2mg sinθ. In order to be at rest, the component of F in the direction perpendicular to OA must balance it, so the magnitude of the component of F perpendicular to OA is at least 2mg sinθ. Since the magnitude of any force is not less than its component in a certain direction, F ≥ 2mg sinθ; when F itself is perpendicular to OA, its magnitude is exactly equal to this component, obtaining the minimum value. Substituting θ=30°, we get F_min=2mg sin30°=mg.
